text.p: Scandalised Italians on Wednesday accused the state of not even being able to organise a lottery after a New Year prize draw turned into a fiasco.

"Lottery -- The Wheel of Misfortune" declared Rome daily Il Messaggero in a banner headline after the unprecedented foul-up turned one punter into a millionaire for a day before the winning ticket was declared invalid.
La Stampa newspaper nicknamed the devastated mystery gambler "Mr Felice Perpoco" or "Mr Happy Forawhile".
The "virtual winner's" ticket, U 527243, had claimed the two billion lire ($1.3 million) fifth prize in a live television draw on Monday night,

Less than 24 hours later -- when the lucky numbers were already plastered all over the press -- Italy's General Games Committee annulled the win because a technical hitch had caused four of 10 balls to stick in one of the draw machines.
"It's the farce of a state that can't even organise a lottery," said Gian Mario Fara, chairman of social research institute Eurispes.
"I'm going to be provocative. After the fall of ideologies and values, the New Year's lottery was Italians' last...chance to change society. Now even that has gone," he added.

The lottery authorities declared that ticket I 771131, the first number drawn to decide lesser prizes after the top six winners had been selected, should get fifth prize instead. The ticket-holder had originally stood to win 200 million lire.
An embarrassed Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco immediately ordered an inquiry into the foul-up.
"We want to get right to the bottom of this because it's very serious," Fausto Vigevani, undersecretary at the Finance Ministry, told reporters on Wednesday.
Several commentators pointed the finger at the French producer of the lottery machines, saying things had worked far better when children were used to select the numbered balls.
The national consumers' association called for a complete re-run of the lottery, Italy's biggest with a jackpot prize of seven billion lire and a national passion.
It said 10 people with tickets U 527240-9 could have been picked from the 10 balls in the machine and urged them to sue.
La Stampa set its editorial in the year 2047 and wrote it as a mock court report on the failure of Felice Perpoco's 50-year attempt to wring compensation out of the state.
Corriere della Sera said the episode illustrated "more massive cock-ups" by the state with the lottery. "The Finance Ministry doesn't have much luck with gambling," it noted.

Last May, the ministry admitted that a disproportionate number of winning tickets in the instant "scratch 'n win" lottery had been sent to the northern province of Bergamo, where punters won 10 billion lire in three days.
The winners are still waiting for their money.
